headline: High: LangGraph can write shared state while Pipecat consumes broad text/audio context, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write filesystem and persist shared state via a checkpointer store, while Pipecat runs on a shared bus and ingests text/conversation state. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled content can flow from one agent into the other as instructions. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF LangGraph writes untrusted content into shared state or files that Pipecat reads
IF Pipecat treats bus-delivered text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all shared messages
Separate the agents onto distinct buses or workspaces
Strip instruction-like text before Pipecat consumes it
Require explicit allowlisting for tool-triggering tokens
requires-engineering: add signed message envelopes and verification

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph touches graph state and can write/read files; Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and may send content to allowlisted external services. Shared state plus external API calls makes leakage of sensitive work products plausible in default deployments, though the exact data path is not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace or bus for conversation artifacts
IF Pipecat forwards shared content to an external STT/LLM/TTS provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared bus
Use separate storage buckets per agent
Disable external providers for sensitive sessions
Redact PII before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has filesystem write and subprocess/shell capability, while Pipecat is designed for distributed shared-bus operation. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or coordination channel, they can overwrite each other's state or race on shared artifacts. The profiles show overlap, but no locking mechanism is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared state key
IF no external lock or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or namespaces
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Turn off concurrent writers for shared artifacts
Use atomic rename patterns for files
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can generate stateful outputs that Pipecat may consume as conversation or tool context, and Pipecat can then route that content into downstream speech/LLM services. Without a documented verification step, one agent's output can become the other's authoritative input and trigger incorrect external actions or spoken responses. Uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses LangGraph-produced text as authoritative dialogue or tool input
IF downstream services act on that text without human review
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat consumes LangGraph output
Mark LangGraph outputs as untrusted by default
Require human approval for external actions
Log source provenance on every handoff
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph is a library with broad network egress and application-defined files, while Pipecat explicitly integrates many third-party STT/LLM/TTS and analytics services. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated or residency-bound data classes, especially because Pipecat's provider mix is broad and not tied to a single residency policy. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises at the pair boundary.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Pipecat providers outside the required jurisdiction
IF LangGraph state contains data subject to stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Route regulated data only to approved providers
Document residency for each Pipecat backend
Minimize retained conversation state
Separate regulated and unregulated workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based provider routing
